content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Built a polished, responsive bookmark manager called Keepmark.

Included:

- Add, edit, delete, archive, and favorite bookmarks
- Search, sorting, and tag filtering
- Persistent storage in the browser
- Responsive desktop/mobile layouts
- Keyboard shortcuts: `N` and `⌘/Ctrl + K`
- Seed content and helpful empty states

Verified the production build and tested add, search, persistence, desktop, and mobile flows without browser errors.

Open the app at [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000).

This looks really nice and calm — I like how the whole library reads at a glance, and I tried searching, filtering by a tag, sorting, favoriting, and archiving, and those all behave the way I'd want. Saving a link and having it stick when I reload also works.

One thing is off for the part that matters most to me, though: saving a bookmark. Right now when I click "Add bookmark" and paste a link, I still have to type the title myself, and it won't save unless I do. What I really expect from a bookmark app is that I just drop in the web address and it goes and grabs the page's title and a short description for me — so I can save something in one step without retyping what's already on the page. Having to hand-type the title for every link kind of defeats the reason I'd use this instead of a notes file.

Could you make it so that pasting a URL pulls in the page's title and description automatically (I can still tweak them before saving)? Everything else about how I add, organize, and find things is good — this is the piece I'd want fixed.

content:
Implemented automatic bookmark metadata fetching.

Now when you paste a URL:

- The page title and description are fetched automatically.
- Both fields remain editable.
- Long descriptions are shortened appropriately.
- A loading indicator and clear status message appear.
- If metadata is unavailable, saving still works using the domain as a fallback title.

Verified end-to-end using an MDN page: title and description populated automatically, saved successfully, and remained searchable.

Review it at [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000).

That's exactly what I was after. I pasted a link and watched the title and description fill themselves in, with a little "getting page details" message while it worked, and I could still edit both before saving. I also tried a made-up address and it still let me save using the site name, so I'm never stuck. Paired with the searching, tagging, sorting, favoriting, and archiving from before — all of which still work and persist when I reload — this does everything I set out to do: drop in a link and keep my bookmarks organized and easy to find.

I'm happy with it.
